I'm fairly new to running, started running in late june early july, didn't really get serious about it until November when I went on my first trail run.. I'm starting off with a trail running 5k in March, and I'm debating on skipping a trail running 10k and going straight for the half. I'm not a strong runner yet, but is it possible? Anyone done this before?

Don't know much about how much easier softer trail-running surface is on your knees, but in my experience running on tarmac you really got to ease into in. Let your body adjust itself to the strain, and thus don't injure yourself.

I started running 5-10k after a few years off of running, but keeping my endurance up with cycling, and ended up rather quickly with painful and swolen knees. Immediately after I noticed, I cut back on running and increased gym-time, doing legpress, squats and lunges. Now virtually painless, after a few months.

So start out small, and grow if it feels ok.

Trail running is a lot easier on the joints than road running in my experience. I even have more endurance on dirt and gravel and whatnot than I do on asphalt, plus down hill is always a hoot lmao. I've just started adding some strength training to my training regimen so hopefully it helps!
